name: Circinus
geometry_note: Complete extended disk and surrounding starfield are in frame. Masked the brightest obvious on-disk foreground stars and reran AutoProf; diffuse major axis and outer ellipse remain plausible. Extreme Galactic foreground crowding persists throughout the galaxy, and large external mask coverage plus foreground extinction and high inclination severely limit arm interpretation. Numerous faint compact sources remain; never identify their Fourier ridges as physical arms. q is an approximate morphology-based thin-disk value with unmodeled foreground/dust/thickness systematics. Numerical measurements, if supported, require strong contamination cautions and an independently visible arm match.

name: Cygnus A
geometry_note: Full host and ample surrounding sky are in the 512-pixel FITS field. Nine visually identified compact field sources overlapping the host were masked and AutoProf rerun. Smooth host envelope is approximately round; q and formal thin-disk inclination are descriptive isophote quantities, not a measured physical disk inclination. No resolved whole-disk arms are apparent. This full-host image cannot supply a comparable pitch for the nuclear spiral confined within 2.25 arcsec; preserve gallery and automated diagnostics but exclude from meaningful whole-disk main-spiral comparisons.
special_case: Paper pitch is nuclear spiral at radius <2.25 arcsec; not galaxy-wide disc spiral; special case.
whole_disk_exclusion_reason: Nuclear-only spiral target (<2.25 arcsec) is not measurable as a whole-disk spiral in this full-host image.

name: ESO558-G009
geometry_note: Full native image frames the galaxy and surrounding sky, but foreground stars dominate the fitted isophotes. The real diffuse galaxy is elongated approximately north-south. Initial AutoProf fit was nearly circular; explicit masks for adjacent bright star, central superposed stars and other field sources, a fixed target WCS center, and a test extending to fainter outer isophotes still produced visibly wrong near-round/oblique fits that miss the extended disk. The latest q and formal inclination are rejected algorithmic diagnostics, not a disk measurement. No forced geometry or Fourier pitch is supplied. No mass targets or published pitches were read.

name: IC 2560
geometry_note: Whole galaxy framed; restored disconnected disk pixels and explicitly masked foreground stars. Outer ellipse follows elongated disk, high inclination/crowding/low contrast limit morphology.

name: J0437+2456
geometry_note: Full compact inclined disk in frame; low-SNR outskirts and high inclination visibly amplify interpolation and noise on deprojection. Ellipse centered and aligned with disk. Spiral morphology may be unresolved/ambiguous, retained with flags rather than inclination exclusion.
original_visual_review_note: The compact inclined disk is weakly resolved, with stretched noise/interpolation and masked point sources apparent after deprojection. Neither the m=2 (+16.4 deg) winding curve nor the near-radial m=4 (+77.3 deg) ridges can be followed along a genuine continuous arm in the observed or deprojected frame. Chirality is unresolved. High inclination is retained as a flag; rejection is due to missing image-level arm correspondence, not an inclination threshold.

name: Milky Way
special_case: Internal observer; no external whole-disc image; keep accounted separately.

name: Mrk 1029
geometry_note: Full galaxy in frame with ample sky. Center and outer ellipse plausible; compact bright core dominates, faint low-contrast outer features and nearby point sources make arm identification uncertain. No crop/truncation.
original_visual_review_note: Compact bright nucleus and smooth diffuse oval dominate the fitted disk. A few outer knots/point-like sources are present, but no coherent arm ridge or reliable winding sign is resolved. The stable m=3 (-65.0 deg) and m=5 (+53.5 deg) curves traverse smooth light/noise rather than follow identifiable arms; their opposite signs cannot be resolved from the image. Neither is image-consistent. Numerical stability alone is insufficient.

name: NGC 0224
geometry_note: The full M31 field and surrounding sky are framed; this is not a crop-truncation failure. Actual final QA shows the strongly elongated galaxy but AutoProf fits an almost round background-scale ellipse (q about 0.926), even after target-mask restoration and an image-based outer-radius/faint-isophote attempt. The coarse Pan-STARRS HiPS image has severe diffuse-light/background limitations. Acquisition trials recorded inadequate Legacy coverage and incomplete SDSS coverage; the available Pan-STARRS field does not recover reliable whole-disk geometry with this pipeline. Mark as unreliable_geometry/image_background. No disk inclination or pitch is reported. This is a limitation of these images and this method, not a claim that M31 lacks spirals or that published pitches are invalid.

name: NGC 0253
geometry_note: Cleaner SkyMapper r whole-disk image selected. Thin outer ellipse follows full high-inclination disk; dust, star crowding and vertical structure strongly limit deprojection.
original_visual_review_note: The highly inclined disk is genuinely clumpy and dusty, but the deprojected image stretches disk texture and residual foreground sources. A coherent main-arm winding cannot be followed securely across the measured annulus. Stable candidates m=2 (+13.4 deg), m=3 (-22.9 deg), m=4 (-11.1 deg), and m=5 (+52.0 deg) cross patchy light without consistently tracking continuous arm ridges. No image-consistent stable main mode is accepted. The approximately 78-degree inclination is a sensitivity flag, not the rejection criterion.

name: NGC 1068
geometry_note: Full disk and sky margin retained. Bright foreground star manually masked; saturated core uses explicitly fixed catalogue-WCS center. Near-circular outer isophotes make photometric PA/inclination weakly constrained; inner and outer structure differ, so this is an outer-disk photometric geometry, not kinematic inclination.

name: NGC 1097
geometry_note: Complete disk with generous margin. Interacting companion near(990,1072) masked manually and AutoProf rerun. Masked area visible; main arms mostly preserved. Strong bar, companion, foreground contamination and large-scale background residuals remain caveats for outer geometry and Fourier modes.

name: NGC 1300
geometry_note: Complete well-resolved barred spiral, correctly centered, arms retained by mask; outer isophote ellipse follows apparent disk. Strong bar/ring morphology can bias thin-disk inclination; retain inclination and geometry-sensitivity flags.

name: NGC 1320
geometry_note: Full inclined disk centered with margin. Nearby bright galaxy at top is masked, though diffuse halo/background contamination may remain. Thin disk fit traces elongated outer profile; low-contrast spiral structure and high inclination are cautions.
original_visual_review_note: A strong smooth oval disk surrounds a bright nucleus and short tight inner dust/arc features. The sole stable candidate, m=6 at +70.7 deg, consists of nearly radial ridges crossing smooth disk light; these do not trace the visible inner structure or any resolved outer arm. Main-disk winding is not securely identified. High inclination and nearby-galaxy halo contamination are cautions, not categorical exclusions. No image-consistent stable main candidate.

name: NGC 1398
geometry_note: Full well-resolved disk and ample sky, correct center. Outer ellipse encloses ring/spiral pattern and most faint branches; central connected arms retained, foreground masks mostly outside disk. Strong ring/bar and variable arm structure retained as morphology caution.
original_visual_review_note: The well-resolved disk contains genuine tightly wound, knotty spiral branches around the central bar/ring. Visible ridges wind clockwise outward in the displayed deprojected coordinates (negative signed pitch). The stable m=6 +16.7 deg candidate has opposite chirality and crosses the branch pattern. The same-chirality stable m=4 -19.7 deg overlay is too open/poorly phased across the nested tight ridges: it moves between bright branches and into smooth outer regions rather than following a coherent main arm across the fitted radial span. Thus neither displayed best stable run is accepted; this is a model-to-image mismatch, not an absence of spiral structure.

name: NGC 2273
geometry_note: Complete disk with sky margin; foreground point sources near outer ring manually masked and AutoProf rerun. Center and disk ellipse plausible. Strong bar, ring structure, high inclination and residual stellar halos can contaminate modes.
original_visual_review_note: The frame shows a bright central bar/inner ring and two broad, low-contrast outer arc/ring segments with knotty portions. Their winding is not securely distinguishable from a closed/pseudoring at this display quality. Stable m=5 (+27.3 deg) and m=6 (-18.0 deg) have isolated overlaps with bright arcs but put multiple additional ridges through the broad smooth interarm disk. Neither supplies a coherent main-arm correspondence over its displayed best stable run. Chirality retained as unknown rather than inferred from the numerical peaks.

name: NGC 2748
geometry_note: Full disk centered and aligned, with bright foreground stars manually masked and geometry refitted. High inclination and strong dust structure make deprojection unstable; retained with explicit caution, not excluded.
original_visual_review_note: Resolved clumps and irregular dust structure are present in the inclined disk, but the deprojection leaves strong asymmetric/lobed diffuse light and vertically stretched features. The sole stable m=1 (-9.5 deg) curve runs around the lower diffuse-light envelope and then through the left outer masked/noisy region; it does not follow a continuous resolved spiral ridge. A reliable common main-arm winding sign cannot be established. Inclination/dust are flags rather than the rejection rule; no image-consistent stable candidate survives.

name: NGC 2960
geometry_note: Original3sigma fit stopped inside visible outer extensions. Mass-blind1sigma refit now includes the full low-contrast disk/arms; foreground stars manually masked. Asymmetric diffuse extensions and low outer SNR make photometric inclination uncertain, retained as a caution.
original_visual_review_note: The expanded fit includes diffuse asymmetric outer extensions with broadly positive winding, especially the right-side loop and upper-left extension; this sign is less secure than for a high-contrast grand-design disk. The stable m=3 +34.3 deg pattern has partial overlap but its three ridges do not jointly trace the actual broad asymmetric features, including a left/lower curve crossing smooth light and masked foreground-source regions. The m=5 -53.9 deg and nearly radial m=6 -83.8 deg candidates are opposite-handed and unsupported. The strong two-sided appearance is not rescued by the numerically unstable m=2 sequence. No image-consistent best stable run is accepted. Low outer SNR and geometry sensitivity remain cautions.

name: NGC 2974
geometry_note: Complete disk with margin. Bright foreground star/spike through inner disk manually masked and outer fit rerun. Outer ellipse plausible, but smooth spheroid-dominated light and weak ring structure make main spiral identification uncertain. Large masked inner region and residual point sources remain cautions.
special_case: Ambiguous E/S0/spiral morphology; retain published sample membership.
original_visual_review_note: The deprojected disk is predominantly smooth with faint ring-like ripples and scattered compact sources; a large foreground-star mask removes part of the inner disk. None of the stable m=1 (+1.3 deg), m=3 (+7.7 deg), m=4 (-12.9 deg), or m=5 (+9.4 deg) curves follows a resolved coherent arm. Their many loops/ridges mostly cross smooth light and point-source locations, so numerical radial stability is not evidence of a main spiral. Disk chirality is unknown. Faint ring structure is acknowledged; no stable spiral match is accepted.

name: NGC 3031
geometry_note: Cleaner SDSS g selected after comparison with Legacy and PanSTARRS failures. Whole disk framed; plausible outer ellipse and visible arms. Diagonal sky seams remain around outer disk, high inclination and weak outer light flagged.

name: NGC 3079
geometry_note: Complete elongated optical galaxy and sky margins are visible. Masked on-disk point sources and the bright saturated stellar core/linear trail southwest of the nucleus; AutoProf rerun. Outer ellipses align with the long diffuse disk and give plausible projected geometry. Very high inclination, strong dust asymmetry, finite thickness and possible warp make thin-disk deprojection highly sensitive. The stretched image contains no unambiguous full main arms by itself; high inclination alone is not an exclusion. Existing fit warnings and perturbation results must accompany any Fourier diagnostic.

name: NGC 3227
geometry_note: Full interacting system and outer sky are visible. Original outer ellipse fitted both target and companion and was rejected. Masked separate bright companion centered near (935,1132) to its visible envelope, plus compact field stars; refit now follows the target disk. Fixed target WCS center was already required by masked core. Target outer projected shape is plausible, but tidal distortion, residual companion halo, dust and the large missing companion sector make q only an approximate disk geometry; angular support guard must decide Fourier availability. Arms in the overlapping sector are unobservable, not reconstructed.

name: NGC 3368
geometry_note: Complete galaxy, faint outer envelope and ample sky are contained. Masked clear compact stellar contaminants including the bright source at the southeast edge; AutoProf rerun. Outer disk ellipse and center match the diffuse oval envelope, and deprojection is plausible. Prominent central oval/bar and near-ringlike outer arms require care: reject modes tracing bar or extra ridges instead of physical arms. Some compact nonstellar-looking arm knots were intentionally preserved. Thin-disk inclination is model-dependent and close to the high-inclination flag threshold.

name: NGC 3393
geometry_note: Full disk and sky margin inspected. Compact foreground stars and a thin linear imaging trail are masked. Restored the contiguous northeast outer arm accidentally removed by generic source segmentation using a local image-defined polygon, retaining invalid data and reapplying explicit stellar masks. Rerun geometry is consistent with the near-circular diffuse outer envelope. q=1 is a boundary-valued fit; PA is weakly constrained and formal i=0 is not evidence of an exactly face-on disk. Bar, broken ring and outer spiral structure are preserved; any genuine-arm match must be judged separately.

name: NGC 3627
geometry_note: Complete optical envelope with sky margin is visible; faint outskirts are contained in the native field. Masked saturated stellar source and its trail, bright edge source and compact stars; retained existing detector/artifact mask south of core. AutoProf refit gives a plausible outer projected disk, with barred/disturbed inner arms. Outer ellipse extends beyond the strong main-arm light, so fixed-radius windows contain a substantial faint-envelope portion. High inclination, dust and asymmetry are flags rather than automatic exclusion. Deprojected margin includes blank pixels outside the native image but the fitted disk is inside the original field.

name: NGC 4151
geometry_note: Full faint outer disk now preserved after restoring disconnected outer-arm pixels; radius initialization500px is image-guided to include visible outer disk rather than only bright inner oval. Weak asymmetric outer light, bar/oval and nuclear brightness make geometry uncertain; accepted diagnostically with flags.
special_case: Published pitch measured in 21cm radio, not optical.
original_visual_review_note: The restored field shows a bright inner barred/oval component and much fainter asymmetric outer extensions, including a lower extended arm. The outer winding is broadly negative, although low surface brightness and separation from the bright inner structure limit confidence. Stable m=1 -3.0 deg gives repeated nearly circular loops across the bar and empty interarm regions. Stable m=4 +27.5 deg is opposite-handed. Stable m=5 -29.6 deg has occasional local alignment but several extra ridges cross smooth light/foreground-star positions and do not trace the faint principal outer extensions over the best stable run. Some faint extension lies beyond the fixed fitted radius; no radius or phase was changed to chase it. No image-consistent stable main candidate is accepted.

name: NGC 4258
geometry_note: Cleaner SDSS g selected. Whole disk and margin visible; plausible outer high-inclination ellipse. Companion masked, mild sky gradients and patchy asymmetric arms flagged.

name: NGC 4303
geometry_note: Complete disk and surrounding sky in frame; fit encloses resolved arm region; centered correctly; mostly near-circular outer isophotes. Mask preserves central connected arms. Some faint outer knots masked; retain mask-dilation sensitivity check. Thin-disk inclination is photometric, not kinematic.

name: NGC 4388
geometry_note: Whole inclined disk in frame. AutoProf overran image boundary; outer geometry now restricted to fully contained fitted isophotes. Extremely high inclination and dust mean deprojected smooth/bar structure cannot establish physical spiral arms; retain as strongly flagged diagnostic.
original_visual_review_note: The highly inclined image resolves inner dust and compact disk features, but the fitted deprojection produces broadly smooth outer light and strongly stretched point sources. No coherent outer arm ridge or secure winding sign is traceable. The stable m=1 +16.9 deg curve crosses the lower diffuse disk without arm correspondence; m=4 +87.1 deg gives near-radial spokes through smooth light. Both are rejected on image mismatch, not by the inclination value.

name: NGC 4395
geometry_note: Full clumpy low-surface-brightness disk restored inside600px; mask no longer removes disconnected outer arms. Isophotal q is uncertain for irregular patchy light and foreground contamination; retain high-inclination flag.
original_visual_review_note: Patchy asymmetric arms and large star-forming complexes are resolved. The dominant upper extension and opposite lower branch broadly wind counterclockwise outward in the displayed deprojection (positive signed pitch), but are far from a uniform symmetric logarithmic pattern. Stable m=1 +2.1 deg and m=2 +6.5 deg are much too tightly wound and repeatedly cross the open/clumpy pattern; m=5 -12.9 deg is opposite-handed. Stable m=6 +43.4 deg gives occasional alignments but also several ridges through obvious interarm gaps/empty outer disk; it does not provide a coherent main-arm match. All displayed best stable runs are rejected, while the genuine irregular spiral morphology is retained.

name: NGC 4501
geometry_note: Whole disk well framed and resolved, mask preserves connected spiral structure. Center and outer-disk ellipse plausible. Inclination around60deg and strong dust lanes cause deprojection/arm-contrast uncertainty; retained with flags.
original_visual_review_note: The disk has prominent resolved flocculent/multi-branch spiral and dust structure, winding clockwise outward in the displayed deprojection (negative signed pitch). The sole same-sign stable candidate, m=1 -6.7 deg, is an almost ring-like single winding that crosses separate arm branches and extends through smooth outer light rather than tracing a coherent main ridge. The m=5 +20.2 deg candidate winds in the opposite direction and adds unsupported ridges. Neither displayed best stable run is image-consistent despite the clear spiral morphology.

name: NGC 4594
geometry_note: Full Sombrero galaxy in frame. Outer isophotes are dominated by the round spheroid, so acos(q)≈52deg is NOT a valid disk inclination: the thin dust disk is visibly much closer to edge-on. Retain this fit only as an explicitly invalid disk-geometry diagnostic; no main spiral should be inferred from smooth bulge light.
original_visual_review_note: A thin dust disk crosses a smooth dominant spheroid; spiral chirality is not observable here. The fitted q=0.621 and acos(q)=51.6 deg describe spheroid-dominated isophotes and are explicitly not a reliable disk inclination, as the geometry review already states. Stable m=3 +7.9 deg loops and m=5 +64.4 deg spokes cross smooth spheroid light and do not match physical disk arms. No main spiral is accepted; retain numerical outputs only with invalid-disk-geometry/morphology cautions.

name: NGC 4699
geometry_note: Full outer disk comfortably framed, explicit foreground-star mask verified. Outer ellipse plausible; tightly wound low-contrast inner structure and bright central component limit spiral interpretation.
original_visual_review_note: Fine inner spiral/dust texture has broadly negative winding around the bright central component, surrounded by a large smooth outer disk. The sole stable m=3 -12.2 deg candidate is same-handed but its displayed 0.40-1.00R-phase curves traverse smooth outer light for much of the radial span and cross rather than track the fine inner branches. Any inner local overlap is insufficient to establish a main-arm match over the best stable run. No stable candidate accepted; do not infer an outer spiral solely from the numerical plateau.

name: NGC 4736
geometry_note: Disconnected outer ring restored; image-guided outer initial radius600 now includes whole outer structure. Fitted ellipse plausible for outer ring but inner/outer geometry differs, negative sky patches and ring morphology strongly limit pitch interpretation.

name: NGC 4826
geometry_note: Whole galaxy in frame with sky margin. Center and outer disk ellipse plausible; faint smooth outer disk dominates fitted geometry while strong asymmetric dust/spiral structure is confined to central region. High inclination and radial morphology changes are cautions.
special_case: Published pitch measured in 21cm radio, not optical.
original_visual_review_note: No stable candidate survives the predeclared radial-stability rules (stable_candidates returned an empty list and render_stable emitted no image). The observed/deprojected disk is smooth over most of the fitted optical annulus, with inner dust structure confined near the bright center. Default mode curves do not follow a resolved whole-disk arm pattern, and main-disk chirality is unknown. No nuclear dust feature is substituted for an optical main spiral.

name: NGC 4945
geometry_note: Whole inclined disk framed with margin, but extremely crowded foreground star field, dust lanes and residual bleed/background artifacts severely contaminate deprojection. Outer ellipse aligned to disk, yet numerical modes must be treated as low-confidence diagnostics; no automatic inclination exclusion.
original_visual_review_note: Fourier computation failed the predeclared radial-support guard: at least 24 supported log-radius samples and at least 75 percent supported rings in a window were required; the log reports Insufficient supported radial rings in window. The whole inclined disk is framed, but extremely crowded foreground stars, extensive masks, dust lanes, and residual streak/bleed artifacts severely compromise disk coverage and deprojection. No reliable whole-disk arm winding can be established from the available image. No pitch or numerical stable candidate is available; retain the computation failure as invalid rather than relax support thresholds or force a value. High inclination is a caution, not the failure criterion.

name: NGC 5055
geometry_note: Whole disk framed, two saturated foreground stars explicitly masked. Major horizontal sky-offset seam crosses outer disk; resulting geometry is diagnostic with strong background-artifact flag. No alternate source accepted.

name: NGC 5495
geometry_note: Whole disk and sky margin present; saturated foreground star and nearby source explicitly masked, with missing arm section retained as mask. Outer round disk plausible but inclination weakly constrained; clear ring/spiral visible.
original_visual_review_note: The two prominent arms have positive winding. The default-annulus m=2 overlay (+27.8 deg) traces these main arms reasonably well and remains an independent automatic comparison, but m=2 has no qualifying predeclared stable run. The displayed stable m=4 (+20.7 deg) and m=6 (+22.9 deg) candidates overlap portions of the arms while adding multiple ridges through smooth interarm light. Those additional ridges are not established physical arms merely because they are harmonics. Reject both as whole-pattern main-arm matches. The upper-left arm is interrupted by a bright foreground-star mask; the numerical stability rule is not relaxed.

name: NGC 5765b
geometry_note: Interacting pair fully framed. Companion masked with explicit elongated aperture; target outer ellipse plausible, but overlap removes substantial upper-arm area and interaction makes deprojection uncertain.
original_visual_review_note: Fourier computation failed the predeclared radial-support guard: at least 24 supported log-radius samples and at least 75 percent supported rings in a window are required; the log reports Insufficient supported radial rings in window. The interacting pair is fully framed. The explicit elongated companion mask crosses a substantial portion of the target upper disk/arm and becomes a broad stripe through the deprojection. The remaining target is asymmetric, dusty, and partly obscured, so no reliable whole-disk winding is assigned. No numerical Fourier peaks or stable candidates were emitted, and no pitch is available. Retain this support failure as invalid rather than relax the guard or force a value. Inclination and interaction are additional geometry caveats, not categorical rejection rules.

name: NGC 6264
geometry_note: Whole disk framed, outer ellipse plausible; two foreground stars explicitly masked. Thin horizontal detector artifact remains across upper disk, weak arms and central bar flagged.

name: NGC 6323
geometry_note: Whole resolved disk well framed; outer ellipse plausible, high inclination and faint outer light flagged. Mask preserves visible inner arm structures.
original_visual_review_note: The compact inclined galaxy has a bright center, short inner arc/dust structure, and a largely smooth outer disk. Neither displayed stable candidate, m=5 (-24.9 deg) nor m=6 (-27.0 deg), tracks a coherent main-arm pattern: their numerous ridges cross smooth outer light and do not correspond to the few inner features. Whole-disk winding is not securely identifiable. No image-consistent stable main mode is accepted.

name: NGC 6926
geometry_note: Whole disturbed disk and sky margin present, outer ellipse plausible but strong asymmetry/interaction makes circular thin-disk assumption uncertain; foreground contamination remains in connected source region.
original_visual_review_note: The dominant left/up and right/down open arms have negative winding. The displayed best stable m=2 run (median -38.7 deg, six neighboring windows, range -39.8 to -34.6 deg) follows those two principal curved arm ridges with consistent handedness over the sampled radial extent. Accept only that displayed m=2 run. The m=4 stable candidate (-43.6 deg) partly tracks the same arms but adds upper/right and lower/left ridges without comparably clear continuous arm correspondence, so m=4 is not accepted. Strong clumps, dust structure, foreground masking, and the approximately 52-degree inclination remain limitations; the main fit is a global approximation rather than a claim that every arm segment is logarithmic.

name: NGC 7582
geometry_note: Full galaxy and sky margin visible. Strong bar/dust and high inclination; outer envelope ellipse plausible, mask preserves connected disk.
original_visual_review_note: There is no numerical stable candidate satisfying the predeclared neighboring-window criterion, so no stable-candidate panel is emitted. The inclined galaxy shows a bar, strong dust, and asymmetric curved structure, but a secure whole-disk main winding is not established from the available overlays. The default-annulus curves do not provide a substitute for the missing stable run. No measurable stable main-arm pitch is accepted; the independent automatic Fourier comparisons remain unchanged.

name: UGC 3789
geometry_note: Whole disk comfortably framed, outer ellipse plausible but near-round geometry gives weak inclination constraint; bright inner ring/bar and faint outer light require morphological caution.
original_visual_review_note: There is no numerical stable candidate satisfying the predeclared neighboring-window criterion, so no stable-candidate panel is emitted. The image is dominated by an inner barred/ring-like structure and a relatively smooth outer disk, with no secure continuous whole-disk main winding. The default-annulus long curves cross smooth outer light rather than demonstrating persistent main-arm ridges. No stable main-arm pitch is accepted; numerical automatic comparisons are retained separately.

name: UGC 6093
geometry_note: Image-guided outer initial radius190 includes outer spiral beyond bright inner ring. Whole galaxy framed, ellipse plausible but bar/ring and irregular outer arms limit thin circular assumption; empirical output-grid PSF unavailable.
